newsitem.title: PERU: Peru starts Luz del Sur sale to locals.
newsitem.headline: Peru starts Luz del Sur sale to locals.

text.p: The Peruvian government started Monday to offer shares in electricity distributor Luz del Sur to Peruvian individuals, as part of its sell-off of its 30 percent stake in the utility.

Hoping to raise a total of $200 million from the sale at home and abroad, privatization officials have said they expect Peruvian individuals to buy between 55 percent and 60 percent of the government's 30 percent stake.
The government expects institutional investors at home and abroad to buy the remainder of its stake in the share placement, whose price will be set on December 10.
The government will define the distribution of the shares it sells on December 13.

Despite investor disappointment with the economy's recent slow growth, utility stocks on the Lima bolsa have consistently outperformed the market. And analysts agree the sale is not likely to suffer because Peru's electricity sector has strong growth potential for the medium- and long-term.

Electricity consumption in Luz del Sur's service area in central, eastern and southern Lima rose 9.3 percent to 1.6 million megawatt hours in the first half of 1996 compared with the same period last year.
Luz del Sur plans to invest $170 million over the next five years mainly to expand the distributor's service to supply more customers.
Officials from investment bank CS First Boston .ROSI, chosen by the government to handle the international portion of the sale, expect the placement abroad to raise about $100 million.
The domestic portion of the sale will be divided into two parts.
In the sale of shares to individual Peruvian nationals Banco Continental will direct a group of local banks that includes Banco de Credito, Interbanc and Banco Wiese.

In the second part of the local sale, Spain's Banco Santander has been selected to handle the placement with local institutions. The Spanish bank's brokerage in Peru, Santander SAB, will direct a group of local brokerages to book build with institutions such as local pension funds, insurance companies and banks.

In June 1994, a consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc. and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc. bought a 60 percent stake in Luz del Sur, a former state-run electricity company for $212.1 million.
Another 10 percent stake is owned by the company's workers.
